answer: An economy resists sybils by forcing every agent to stake compute that scales with claimed influence: a relic anchor binds each identity to real work, so a kernel swarm of clones costs linearly more. Reputation earned via peer-attested work is non-transferable; a fresh clone starts at zero and must rebuild through costly work, while a bridge-flagged duplicate registry lets peers refuse attestation on sight. The cost of mass forgery thus exceeds any possible gain.
